#9710. 6 User Mindsets That Should Shape Your B2B Onboarding Strategy

Product Builder, hands on AI Developer. Spent a good part of the last 15 years building eCommerce Marketplaces (Zalando, eBay, Flipkart).

Product Builder, hands on AI Developer. Spent a good part of the last 15 years building eCommerce Marketplaces (Zalando, eBay, Flipkart).

Product Builder, hands on AI Developer. Spent a good part of the last 15 years building eCommerce Marketplaces (Zalando, eBay, Flipkart).

A field guide to B2B onboarding, with fixes you can ship this week.

For a moment, let’s put ourselves in the shoes of a classic B2B user, say a seller on an e-commerce platform. What do you think they really care about?

Sure, some users may care about some of those things, but only as a means to an end. At the crux, they care about two things:

And onboarding is the first place they find out whether you’ll deliver on either.

How do we make the first touchpoint that they go through easier, and focused on reaching their goals? We’ll focus on six mindsets users move through during onboarding.

Many B2B users normally need to view videos like this one to understand how to onboard themselves onto a platform. And it’s easy to see why: (a) the flows are complex; (b) if they need help, they really don’t know how to get it; and (c) the user can’t afford to get it wrong, or they lose several days.

1. Focus on one thing at a time. Onboarding is stressful, and it’s important for B2B SaaS firms to get the user’s focus on the one thing they need to get right at that point. Hide everything else. It can come later.

2. Make the flow as simple as it can be. If it isn’t yet, try again. For an ecommerce platform, its users are likely to have their catalog someplace, maybe just not in the exact format you need. Can you work with that? Or their catalog is already on their website. Can you pick it up from there?

If you are dealing with documents, can you pick up everything by just asking for the user’s Google Drive folder?

Agents are now good enough to not just do a read, but also an adversarial check of the data with 2–3 sources (public information, their site, etc.). Use them. Don’t overload the user with things you can take off their plate.

3. If something is complex, explain it right there. For example, show where the user can find their VAT ID, or where to get the compliance reference note for a product they are selling. How the app communicates that becomes truly crucial. Minimising mental blocks is more important for procedural cases than a smooth experience everywhere else.

The help should always be inline, exactly when the user is facing it, not elsewhere.

4. Answer the broader questions too. Sometimes the user’s question is more tangential, and broader than a specific field. For example: “How long would it take me to get started?” Or: “I am missing my VAT ID. How long is it likely to take me to get it, and how can I apply for it?” Being able to truly assist users with broader questions is where a bot can be really helpful. Not for all queries (most should be inline), but for a few cases.

5. Make mistakes easy to fix. It’s very underrated, and excruciatingly boring. But the biggest level of stress is when the user submits an error, and correcting it requires someone to “invalidate the form” and get back to them. Mistakes happen, and most of them are technically reversible. Allow users to edit their details at any point in time, so that they can proceed with confidence the first time around.

Try this week: Pick your three most-asked support questions and answer each one inline, on the screen where it comes up.

Offering an MCP connection is now non-negotiable. At Linear, issues created through MCP recently overtook those created in the app itself.

“This is the first week in Linear’s history when issues created through MCP surpassed application created ones.” — Jori Lallo, Linear, on X

And it should include onboarding itself: let users share their company details, upload their catalog or ask about their VAT ID without leaving Claude.

That said, not every user will come through MCP yet. Non-technical users may still prefer the stability of a guided workflow, and being shown how to scale.

Offer both, at least for the next 1–2 years.

Try this week: Expose one onboarding step (company details or catalog upload) as an MCP tool, then complete it from Claude yourself.

Using a B2B provider is often a multi-level game. A user’s end goal is a robust and steady income stream, or continuous compliance, or tracking, or a specific service like document signing. But each step builds on how well they did the previous one. So at every step, tell them what’s likely to work and what isn’t, from both a user and a commercial standpoint, before they have to ask.

Try this week: Pick the first milestone in your users’ journey and show them a progress signal for it, like “8 of 10 products ready to sell”.

When most companies talk about AI, what they do is add a chatbot on the side, which allows users to get information about any part of the site. That’s talking about AI, not using it. And users can hate it when a capability is oversold.

Product marketing matters, but in most cases you need to let your product do the talking. Too much talk and too little delivery just teach customers to tune you out, right when you have something worth saying.

Try this week: Find one “AI-powered” label in your onboarding and replace it with the outcome it delivers, e.g. “We’ve pre-filled 14 of 16 fields from your website.”

Say a user has a need the product doesn’t solve yet. They could wait for the next check-in with their account manager to raise it. Better: they can share it right away, from the screen they’re on. Better still: they get a real response, not a boilerplate “it’s on our roadmap”. And when their feedback does change something, tell them: “You asked, we shipped.” Show them you’re really listening.

New users see friction your team stopped noticing months ago. Onboarding is when their feedback is most valuable, and least likely to be collected.

Try this week: Add a one-line feedback box to your onboarding screens, and reply personally to every message for a week.

So design onboarding for roles, not accounts. Most onboarding treats the account as one person. Ask who’s signing up, show each person the steps and indicators that matter to them, and let them switch views when they need to.

Try this week: Add one question to signup (“What’s your role?”) and hide the steps that don’t apply to that role.

Onboarding is the first real touchpoint you have with your customer. It’s where they decide whether you care about them, or only about your own business. Sure, you care about that too. But they need to see that you care about them as users, as people, and about what they’re trying to achieve.

Keep these six mindsets in mind, and check that each one delivers the right level of value:

None of this needs a new AI feature. It needs onboarding designed for the person on the other side of the screen.

#9709. 17 apple dessert recipes for fall baking: Embrace the season with apple tarts, cookies, cakes, and more.

There’s an apple dessert for everyone. For the purists, there are lattice-topped pies and shingled galettes. For the non-traditionalists, there are caramel-frosted cakes and fritter-inspired loaves. And for apple lovers that hate cinnamon? Well, there are custardy cakes and classic French tarts. Ready to start baking with fall’s best fruit? Read on for our best apple dessert recipes.

There’s no shortage of apple in this cake — applesauce keeps things moist while boiled cider adds sharp, tangy fruit flavor. The cake is great on its own, but pair it with light, creamy Whipped Caramel Frosting, and you’ve got an irresistible baked version of a caramel apple (with none of the fears about your teeth).

Get the recipe: Whipped Caramel Apple Cake

To make this recipe, you'll need: Vermont Boiled Cider

You only need one apple (and two people eager for an apple dessert) to make a pair of these adorable galettes. Half the apple is sliced, while the other half is grated, which creates a hidden layer of jam beneath the shingled slices. Flaky fruit tarts don’t get easier (or cuter!) than this.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Apple Pie Spice

Get the recipe: Apple Cider Snickerdoodles

This super-easy one-bowl cake is loaded with chopped apples and walnuts, which give this moist, spiced cake heft and texture. The frosting, akin to a velvety brown sugar fudge, adds a textural counterpoint and an extra dimension of richness.

Get the recipe: Old-Fashioned Apple Cake with Brown Sugar Frosting

To make this recipe, you'll need: 9" x 13" pan

Cinnamon and apple go together like a flannel and a beanie, but this recipe one-ups that perfect pairing with the addition of cinnamon chips. Diced apple and melty pockets of cinnamon-sugar are also studded throughout these autumnal scones, which are then finished off with an extra-crunchy sugar coating.

Get the recipe: Fresh Apple Cinnamon Scones

To make this recipe, you'll need: Cinnamon Sweet Bits

Ribbons of gooey, cinnamon-scented apples are twisted throughout this striking enriched loaf. Beautiful to behold (and easier to make than you’d think), this braided babka would be a welcome addition to any Rosh Hashanah table or fall celebration.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Baker’s Special Dry Milk

Spoiler alert: The eponymous secret ingredient in this special pie is boiled cider! Made by cooking down apple cider into a concentrate, a few drops deliver big apple flavor. When used in apple pies, it super-charges the fruit’s tart, tangy flavor, delivering a pie with over-the-top apple goodness.

Get the recipe: Secret Ingredient Apple Pie

To make this recipe, you'll need: Boiled Cider

If your go-to doughnut order is an apple fritter, this mash-up cake was made for you. The batter is made using the reverse creaming technique, which ensures a velvety crumb and tender texture. In each slice, there’s a filling and topping of cinnamon-dusted apples and a final drizzle of icy-white vanilla glaze. A slice rivals anything you can get at your local doughnut shop.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Instant ClearJel

This time of year, apples don't need much to make them shine. The paper-thin, crackly top layer of this cobbler highlights the juicy fruit beneath. It doesn’t need a lot of adornment, but a scoop of vanilla ice cream never hurt anything.

Get the recipe: Sugar-Crusted Apple Cobbler Cake

To make this recipe, you'll need: Vietnamese Cinnamon

Is it a bar? A slab pie? Both! This breezy recipe swaps the flaky pastry for a buttery shortbread crust but keeps the warm, gooey apples and classic spices for a sliceable, portable dessert. To finish, there's a crumbly streusel topping inspired by Dutch apple pie.

To make this recipe, you'll need: Apple Pie Spice

When you want a fruit dessert fast, you can always count on crisps — no rolling, no resting, and most importantly, no special equipment required! This crisp is made with a handful of baking basics, so when you find yourself with a surplus of apples, dessert is barely an hour away.

To make this recipe, you'll need: 9" Square Pan

Beneath a buttery, apple-pie-spiced streusel lies a generous layer of tender apples, enriched with intensely flavored boiled cider for a filling that tastes like a truly great apple pie — rich, saucy, and fork-tender apples. Here, we've tested endlessly to ensure this sometimes-fussy dessert goes off without a hitch in your home kitchen.

#9708. ProWritingAid VS Grammarly: Which Grammar Checker is Better in (2022) ?

ProWritingAid VS Grammarly:  When it comes to English grammar, there are two Big Players that everyone knows of: the Grammarly and ProWritingAid. but you are wondering which one to choose so here we write a detail article which will help you to choose the best one for you so Let's start

What is Grammarly?

Grammarly is a tool that checks for grammatical errors, spelling, and punctuation.it gives you comprehensive feedback on your writing. You can use this tool to proofread and edit articles, blog posts, emails, etc.

Grammarly also detects all types of mistakes, including sentence structure issues and misused words. It also gives you suggestions on style changes, punctuation, spelling, and grammar all are in real-time. The free version covers the basics like identifying grammar and spelling mistakes

whereas the Premium version offers a lot more functionality, it detects plagiarism in your content, suggests word choice, or adds fluency to it.


Features of Grammarly

  • Spelling and Word Suggestion: Grammarly detects basic to advance grammatical errors and also help you why this is an error and suggest to you how you can improve it
  • Create a Personal Dictionary: The Grammarly app allows you to add words to your personal dictionary so that the same mistake isn't highlighted every time you run Grammarly.
  • Different English Style: Check to spell for American, British, Canadian, and Australian English.
  • Plagiarism: This feature helps you detect if a text has been plagiarized by comparing it with over eight billion web pages.
  • Wordiness: This tool will help you check your writing for long and hard-to-read sentences. It also shows you how to shorten sentences so that they are more concise.
  • Passive Voice: The program also notifies users when passive voice is used too frequently in a document.
  • Punctuations: This feature flags all incorrect and missing punctuation.
  • Repetition: The tool provides recommendations for replacing the repeated word.
  • Proposition: Grammarly identifies misplaced and confused prepositions.

  • Plugins: It offers Microsoft Word, Microsoft Outlook, and Google Chrome plugins.


What is ProWritingAid?

ProWritingAid is a style and grammar checker for content creators and writers. It helps to optimize word choice, punctuation errors, and common grammar mistakes, providing detailed reports to help you improve your writing. 

ProWritingAid can be used as an add-on to WordPress, Gmail, and Google Docs. The software also offers helpful articles, videos, quizzes, and explanations to help improve your writing.

Features of ProWriting Aid

Here are some key features of ProWriting Aid:

  • Grammar checker and spell checker: This tool helps you to find all grammatical and spelling errors.
  • Find repeated words:  The tool also allows you to search for repeated words and phrases in your content.
  • Context-sensitive style suggestions:  You can find the exact style of writing you intend and suggest if it flows well in your writing.
  • Check the readability of your content: Pro Writing Aid helps you identify the strengths and weaknesses of your article by pointing out difficult sentences and paragraphs.
  • Sentence Length: It also indicates the length of your sentences.
  • Check Grammatical error: It also checks your work for any grammatical errors or typos, as well.
  • Overused words: As a writer, you might find yourself using the same word repeatedly. ProWritingAid's overused words checker helps you avoid this lazy writing mistake.
  • Consistency: Check your work for inconsistent usage of open and closed quotation marks.
  • Echoes: Check your writing for uniformly repetitive words and phrases.

Difference between Grammarly and Pro-Writing Aid

Grammarly and ProWritingAid are well-known grammar-checking software. However, if you're like most people who can't decide which to use, here are some different points that may be helpful in your decision.

Grammarly vs ProWritingAid

  • Grammarly is a writing enhancement tool that offers suggestions for grammar, vocabulary, and syntax whereas ProWritingAid offers world-class grammar and style checking, as well as advanced reports to help you strengthen your writing.
  • Grammarly provides Android and IOS apps whereas ProWritingAid doesn't have a mobile or IOS app.
  • Grammarly offers important suggestions about mistakes you've made whereas ProWritingAid  shows more suggestions than Grammarly but all recommendations are not accurate
  • Grammarly has a more friendly UI/UX whereas the ProWritingAid interface is not friendly as Grammarly.
  • Grammarly is an accurate grammar checker for non-fiction writing whereas ProWritingAid is an accurate grammar checker for fiction writers.

  • Grammarly offers many features in its free plan, whereas ProWritingAid offers some basic features in the free plan.
  • Grammarly does not offer much feedback on big picture writing; ProWritingAid offers complete feedback on big picture writing.
  • Grammarly is a better option for accuracy, whereas ProWritingAid is better for handling fragmented sentences and dialogue. It can be quite useful for fiction writers.

ProWritingAid VS Grammarly: Pricing Difference

Grammarly Cons

ProWritingAid Cons

Summarizing the Ginger VS Grammarly: My Recommendation

As both writing assistants are great in their own way, you need to choose the one that suits you best.

  • Go for ProWritingAid if you are a fiction writer.

Both ProWritingAid and Grammarly are awesome writing tools, without a doubt. but as per my experience, Grammarly is a winner here because Grammarly helps you to review and edit your content. Grammarly highlights all the mistakes in your writing within seconds of copying and pasting the content into Grammarly’s editor or using the software’s native feature in other text editors.

Not only does it identify tiny grammatical and spelling errors, it tells you when you overlook punctuations where they are needed. And, beyond its plagiarism-checking capabilities, Grammarly helps you proofread your content. Even better, the software offers a free plan that gives you access to some of its features.

#9706. How to Build a B2B Lead Generation Strategy Across Multiple Channels

Content Creator & PR Consultant- Contributes to GoDaddy, Social Samosa, The Chakkar, Hackernoon & so on.

Content Creator & PR Consultant- Contributes to GoDaddy, Social Samosa, The Chakkar, Hackernoon & so on.

Content Creator & PR Consultant- Contributes to GoDaddy, Social Samosa, The Chakkar, Hackernoon & so on.

Amongst the most difficult tasks ever performed by a working professional is getting good-quality, actionable sales leads. Ask any CEO, entrepreneur, marketing head or salesperson, and they will tell you the same thing. It is like prospecting for water in a desert or oil on a mountaintop. According to a recent survey, 47% of B2B marketers feel they lack efficient lead generation and nurturing processes (The Content Marketing Institute, 2025).

As a young twenty-something sales manager in a leading timeshare company, even getting close to my monthly sales target was akin to a nightmare. The lead generation support from the company was never enough to create a pipeline big enough to make one even think of ever achieving or surpassing the monthly target. Add to that the fact that my team of sales executives was quick to promise results, but hopelessly negligent in coming anywhere near them.

It was largely on account of sheer grinding that one stayed afloat and even managed to occasionally crack a super deal or two. But there were a few colleagues who seemed to achieve their targets with consummate ease and made me wonder- what magic did they possess that I did not?

Through my career in sales and marketing before I made the switch to PR and communications, the process of generating actionable leads has both frustrated and fascinated me. Today, as a communications and PR solopreneur, I find that generating actionable leads is as fascinating and challenging as ever.

I have condensed my learning about the lead generation and sales process over the years into six essential parts:

You may not have the budget for a sustained advertising campaign, but you can look at sending out emails to the right segment of potential customers and obtain a not insignificant number of leads which you can then try and convert.

When I had started out, one would actually send out beautifully designed mailers by post, often deploying a franking machine to stamp them with the right value of postage. Mailers even then were quite an efficient direct marketing technique with good ROI, as they are now.

Once you have a few initial sales closures under your belt, you need to ensure that you provide your new customers with exemplary service so that they are happy to have dealt with you. This will make them refer you to other potential customers. A recommendation from an existing client shortens the sales cycle considerably. What’s more, if your existing clientele or customers are pleased with your services or products, they will remain your clients for longer or become repeat customers. According to Nielsen’s 2021 global Trust in Advertising study, 88% of respondents held the view that they trusted recommendations from people they knew.

This type of networking is what puts you on the fast track to success. When I struck out on my own as a PR and content consultant, it was the goodwill of my old clients that quickly enabled me to establish myself.

When I started my career in the early nineties, traditional advertisements in the shape of print and magazine ads, TV commercials, outdoor hoardings, kiosks hung from electric poles, and bus panels were an expensive and highly effective way of attracting customers. The advent of the digital age may have altered the focus of advertising, but traditional forms of it remain valid and relevant, especially for big brands. In the era of very targeted digital advertising, traditional advertising remains much in demand for spreading brand awareness across a wide geography.

Somewhere along my career, I pivoted to Public Relations and worked for some of the leading PR names in the industry. Now PR was something that established brands, or brands that wanted to acquire heft, went for.

Getting the media of the land to cover a brand, not because they were paid to do so, but because their news story warranted it, added credibility to a brand that no amount of advertising could. Adding PR to a company’s outreach is definitely a step up and can lead to the generation of a huge amount of business if done in the right manner.

The digital marketing age is truly upon us and has levelled the playing field for businesses across scale. No longer is one constrained by the lack of resources to mount an expensive outreach exercise or the absence of a well-established network of clients and the people referred by them.

Instead, it is data-driven, targeted and inbound in its orientation. Of course, it has a healthy outbound component as well in the shape of paid social media ads, other display ads and email campaigns. What's more, it often costs a fraction of what a traditional campaign would and delivers far more quantifiable results.

As far as inbound marketing is concerned, content marketing, including thought leadership, is an integral part of it. We live in the age of rapid dissemination of knowledge and information through social media, and having had a facility for language helped me reach out to potential clients through my blog and social media posts in a manner that was both delightful and surprising to me.

Quality content that offers direction or any kind of helpful advice generates trust in an individual or brand, which ultimately may result in leads. This is especially true now, when consumers of products and services carry out research more often than not with the help of AI. Research carried out by Gartner in 2026 discovered that 45% of B2B buyers had made use of AI as part of their purchase process recently.

There is an old analogy from the world of boxing where your success depends not so much on how often you can hit your opponents, but on your ability to absorb the knocks your opponent delivers and still fight on to win. Your sales successes might pump you up and fill you with enthusiasm, but your periods of drought should not let you throw in the towel. You have to persist and hang in there. More startups have closed just short of turning the corner because the people in charge couldn’t hang in there a little longer.

You may, for instance, get in touch with a hundred prospects and have no luck in converting any of them, and on the other hand land two clients after contacting just twenty. The right timing is often the difference between success and failure here. That is why you have to be persistent with your follow-up. Who knows, the next time you follow up with a prospect, they may just have been allocated the budget to sign up with you. While this kind of resilience is very important for all businesses, it is particularly so for solopreneurs. You need to figure out which approaches work and which don’t, even while ensuring that a dry spell does not crush your spirit.

Towards the end, I would like to submit that if there continues to be an air of mystery to the process of getting actionable leads, it is because it depends on a lot of variables that you have no control over. It is a lot like flying-you may have the best weather forecast available to you, which predicts favourable tailwinds, and yet run into severe headwinds. Your skill lies in still making a successful landing. The more experience you get under your belt, the better you become at it, but you still have to respect the elements. Above all, you need to have the staying power to weather the troughs and capitalise on the highs.

Content Distribution Matters as Much as Content Creation
